verses.english: “Mendicants, I will teach you the all.

verses.pali: Cakkhuñceva rūpā ca, sotañca saddā ca, ghānañca gandhā ca, jivhā ca rasā ca, kāyo ca phoṭṭhabbā ca, mano ca dhammā ca—
verses.english: It’s just the eye and sights, the ear and sounds, the nose and smells, the tongue and tastes, the body and touches, and the mind and ideas.
Mendicants, suppose someone was to say:

verses.pali: ‘ahametaṁ sabbaṁ paccakkhāya aññaṁ sabbaṁ paññāpessāmī’ti, tassa vācāvatthukamevassa;
verses.english: ‘I’ll deny this all and describe another all.’ They’d have no grounds for that claim,

verses.pali: puṭṭho ca na sampāyeyya, uttariñca vighātaṁ āpajjeyya.
verses.english: they’d be stumped by questions, and, in addition, they’d get frustrated.
Because they’re out of their element.”
